blocks.value: printf() formats output using a format specifier, a placeholder that controls how a value is displayed, like how many decimal places a number shows.
%.2f means: format as a floating-point number (f) with 2 digits after the decimal point.

Specifier   Type            Example
%c          Character       %c, or %2c (in a 2-space field)
%d          Integer         %d
%f          Floating-point  %f, %.2f (2 decimals), %6.2f (2 decimals, 6-space field)
%e          Exponential     %e
%s          String          %s, %10s (10-space field), %.2s (first 2 characters)
